executiveSummary: Analysis of 20 surveillance reports from ECDC and PAHO spanning November 2025 through May 2026 reveals multiple concurrent public health threats across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1), a BSL-3 select agent, has generated two PAHO epidemiological updates indicating sustained zoonotic activity in the Americas region. Concurrent circulation of dengue, chikungunya, mpox, measles, and pertussis reflects significant regional burden, while the start of the Southern Hemisphere influenza season in April 2026 adds additional respiratory disease pressure. The co-circulation of multiple high-impact pathogens across the Americas and Europe represents a complex, multi-threat environment requiring coordinated surveillance and response.
bottomLine: The Americas and Europe face simultaneous elevated threats from H5N1 avian influenza, dengue, mpox, measles, pertussis, and seasonal respiratory viruses, demanding heightened surveillance and cross-border coordination.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Two separate PAHO epidemiological updates issued within months (November 2025, March 2026) indicating sustained and ongoing zoonotic activity
BSL-3 select agent with pandemic potential; continued animal-to-human spillover risk in the Americas region
threats.action: Activate enhanced zoonotic surveillance at human-animal interface; enforce biosafety protocols at poultry farms and live animal markets; expedite antiviral stockpiling and pandemic influenza preparedness planning

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued February 2026 indicating active transmission across multiple countries in the Americas
Historical hyperendemicity combined with ongoing arbovirus co-circulation with chikungunya elevates outbreak risk
threats.action: Intensify vector control operations; strengthen hospital surge capacity for hemorrhagic fever cases; promote community-based Aedes aegypti elimination campaigns

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued April 2026 confirming continued transmission in the Americas
BSL-3 select agent; sustained community transmission signals incomplete control of the ongoing multi-country outbreak
threats.action: Scale up vaccination with MVA-BN vaccine for high-risk populations; enforce contact tracing and isolation protocols; coordinate with CDC and national health authorities for laboratory confirmation and case reporting

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating measles activity in the Americas region
Declining vaccination coverage post-COVID-19 pandemic creates susceptible populations at risk for outbreak amplification
threats.action: Launch emergency vaccination catch-up campaigns targeting under-vaccinated communities; strengthen measles-rubella surveillance and laboratory confirmation capacity; coordinate cross-border response for imported cases

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two PAHO reports issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained and increasing pertussis activity in the Americas
Resurgence pattern consistent with waning immunity and potential vaccine escape strains
threats.action: Reinforce Tdap booster campaigns for adolescents and adults; prioritize vaccination of pregnant women for neonatal protection; investigate potential antimicrobial resistance patterns in circulating strains

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza and Respiratory Virus Co-circulation
signals: PAHO alert on simultaneous influenza and RSV circulation issued January 2026; Southern Hemisphere influenza season start alert issued April 2026
ECDC issued five consecutive weekly communicable disease threat reports (Weeks 16-20, April-May 2026) indicating sustained respiratory disease pressure in Europe
threats.action: Promote annual influenza vaccination; enhance hospital capacity planning for respiratory surge; monitor for novel influenza reassortants given concurrent H5N1 zoonotic activity

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating active chikungunya transmission
Co-circulation with dengue virus complicates clinical diagnosis and may overwhelm healthcare capacity in affected regions
threats.action: Strengthen arboviral syndromic surveillance to differentiate dengue and chikungunya; enhance vector control; ensure diagnostic laboratory capacity for serological and molecular differentiation

threats.name: Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued December 2025 indicating HPS activity in the Americas
High case fatality rate (~35%) and sporadic but unpredictable case clustering in rural rodent-exposure zones
threats.action: Enhance environmental surveillance for rodent reservoir populations; issue public health advisories for high-risk rural occupations; ensure ICU capacity and supportive care protocols at regional hospitals

selectAgentSummary: Two BSL-3 select agents have been identified in these surveillance reports. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) (BSL-3 select agent) generated two PAHO epidemiological updates in November 2025 and March 2026, indicating sustained zoonotic transmission in the Americas with pandemic reassortment risk. Monkeypox virus (MPXV, BSL-3 select agent) generated a PAHO epidemiological update in April 2026 confirming ongoing community transmission in the Americas. Both require enhanced biosafety protocols, specialized laboratory handling, and coordinated national and international response measures.
amrSignals: Pertussis resurgence noted across two PAHO reporting periods (December 2025, March 2026) may reflect waning vaccine-induced immunity or emerging Bordetella pertussis strains with altered antimicrobial susceptibility profiles, warranting systematic antimicrobial resistance surveillance

GLP-1 receptor agonist misuse alert (PAHO, February 2026) raises indirect AMR concern through counterfeit and substandard pharmaceutical supply chains that may co-distribute subtherapeutic antimicrobials
emergingPatterns: Temporal clustering of five consecutive ECDC weekly threat reports (April-May 2026) suggests sustained or escalating communicable disease pressure in Europe entering summer transmission season

Dual PAHO H5N1 updates within four months (November 2025 to March 2026) indicate persistent and potentially expanding avian influenza zoonotic spillover in the Americas, increasing pandemic preparedness urgency
Simultaneous arboviral co-circulation (dengue and chikungunya) combined with Southern Hemisphere influenza season onset creates compounded healthcare system strain risk in tropical Americas
Post-pandemic measles and pertussis resurgence pattern across the Americas is consistent with a global trend of vaccine-preventable disease rebound due to COVID-19-era immunization disruptions
Mpox transitioning from acute outbreak phase to endemic community transmission in the Americas, as evidenced by sustained PAHO monitoring into April 2026
